clue.text: What Sunak will do at election time — leave the city

definitions.text: What Sunak will do at election time
definitions.meaning: a prime minister who calls a general election is said to ..., asking voters to decide
taken literally, heading out of town into rural parts

explanation.surface: A political observation: the prime minister will be leaving London behind when polling day comes.
explanation.walkthrough: Rishi Sunak was the UK prime minister; in British politics a leader who calls an election is said to go to the country.
explanation.definitionFit: The phrase is the idiom for calling a general election, and literally means travelling out into rural areas.

clue.text: Painter wins over Kensington and Chelsea, say

parts.note: to gain something is to win it
Kensington and Chelsea is a London borough, so it is an example of one

explanation.surface: An artist triumphs over a wealthy part of London.
explanation.walkthrough: Kensington and Chelsea is one of the administrative boroughs of London; 'say' marks it as an example.
explanation.definitionFit: Thomas Gainsborough was an eighteenth-century English portrait and landscape artist.

clue.text: Time small town dismisses lead ploughman's work

indicators.note: the small town loses its leading letter, the first one being sent away

parts.note: a village is a small settlement

explanation.surface: A little town gets rid of its leader, perhaps in a farming community.
explanation.walkthrough: 'dismisses lead' takes the V off VILLAGE, leaving ILLAGE.
explanation.definitionFit: Tillage is the cultivation of land by ploughing, exactly what a ploughman does.

clue.text: Group of performers travelling to Peru

indicators.note: letters that are travelling move about, so the letters of the two words are rearranged

explanation.surface: A company of actors on tour, heading to South America.
explanation.walkthrough: 'travelling' rearranges TO PERU.
explanation.definitionFit: A troupe is a company of actors, dancers or other entertainers who perform together.

clue.text: I want more energy and new heart

parts.note: E is the physics symbol for energy
the core of something is its heart or centre

explanation.surface: Someone feels in need of a fresh boost and new courage.
explanation.walkthrough: The definition is what an audience shouts, so it stands as a whole exclamation.
explanation.definitionFit: Audiences call out this word to demand another song or piece after the performance seems to end.

clue.text: Separately, this makes 11

definitions.meaning: writing the figure 1 beside the figure 1 produces 11, read as one placed by one

explanation.surface: A puzzling arithmetic remark about how a number is formed when things are taken apart.
explanation.walkthrough: The second reading is visual: put the digit 1 next to another 1 and you see eleven.
explanation.definitionFit: Doing things individually in sequence, rather than together, is the idiomatic sense of the phrase.

clue.text: Sharp dip made from chopped endives with nothing in

indicators.note: the zero goes in, placed inside the rearranged letters
salad leaves that are chopped are cut up, so the letters of the vegetable are rearranged

parts.note: O looks like zero, meaning nothing

explanation.surface: A recipe for a sharp-flavoured dip made from chopped salad leaves.
explanation.walkthrough: 'chopped' turns ENDIVES into NSEDIVE, and 'in' puts O after its first letter. 'Sharp dip' looks culinary but means a sudden fall.
explanation.definitionFit: A nosedive is a steep plunge, as of an aircraft or of share prices, so a sudden sharp drop.

clue.text: Caviar expensive, it's said? It may be a buck

parts.note: caviar is fish roe

indicators.note: a hint that the word for expensive is only heard, standing for a same-sounding animal

parts.note: something expensive is dear

explanation.surface: A diner remarks that caviar is pricey, then muses about money.
explanation.walkthrough: 'it's said' signals that DEAR is replaced by its sound-alike DEER. 'buck' looks like slang for a dollar, fitting the expensive caviar, but means a male animal.
explanation.definitionFit: A buck is a male deer, and the roe is a small European species whose males are called bucks.

clue.text: Northerner's home including empty bathroom

indicators.note: the word including is emptied of its inner letters, so only its first and last remain

parts.note: loo is British slang for a toilet or bathroom

explanation.surface: An Arctic dwelling that comes with a bathroom nobody uses.
explanation.walkthrough: 'empty' applies to 'including', not to the bathroom: removing its middle leaves IG. 'including' wants to be a containment signal; it is the fodder.
explanation.definitionFit: An igloo is the snow-block dome traditionally built by Inuit people of the far north.

clue.text: The full complement of men on board?

definitions.text: The full complement of men on board?

parts.words: The full complement of men on board?
parts.note: reads like a ship's crew, but the men are pieces and the board is a chessboard

explanation.surface: A question about a ship's full crew.
explanation.walkthrough: Chess pieces are traditionally called men, and the board is the playing board rather than a vessel.
explanation.definitionFit: A complete set of chess pieces is all thirty-two men needed to play a game on the board.

clue.text: Nato articles sorted out disputes

indicators.note: things sorted out are rearranged into a new order, so these letters are reworked

explanation.surface: Clauses of the Atlantic alliance's treaty were thrashed out to settle disagreements.
explanation.walkthrough: 'sorted out' rearranges NATO ARTICLES, twelve letters.
explanation.definitionFit: Altercations are noisy quarrels or heated arguments, so they are disputes.

clue.text: Do without women?

parts.note: do is a party, and one without women is the all-male celebration before a wedding

explanation.surface: A short question about managing without women.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Do' reads as a verb but is the noun meaning a social event.
explanation.definitionFit: A pre-wedding celebration held for the groom and his male friends only is the classic men-only party.

clue.text: Live healthily after start of diet

indicators.note: placed after means the healthy word follows the diet letter
the start of a word is its opening letter, so only the first letter of diet is used

parts.note: to be well is to be healthy

explanation.surface: Advice to live a healthy life once a diet begins.
explanation.walkthrough: 'start of' takes D from diet; 'after' puts WELL behind it.
explanation.definitionFit: To dwell somewhere is to reside or have your home there.

clue.text: Fan missing large part of cricket match

indicators.note: missing means lacking, so the size letter is dropped from the fan word

parts.note: a lover of something is a fan of it

explanation.surface: A supporter who skips a big chunk of a cricket game.
explanation.walkthrough: 'missing' drops L from LOVER. An over in cricket is a set of six balls bowled from one end.
explanation.definitionFit: Cricket play is divided into overs, each a sequence of six deliveries by one bowler.

clue.text: Place to study poetry or the cosmos

parts.note: uni is short for university, a place of study
verse is poetry

explanation.surface: Choosing between a university literature course and astronomy.
explanation.definitionFit: The universe is all of space and everything in it, which the cosmos also names.

clue.text: Wild stare by king and queen for naked intruder

indicators.note: something wild is out of control, so the letters are thrown into a new order

parts.note: K is the chess abbreviation for king
ER, Elizabeth Regina, stands for the queen

explanation.surface: Royals react with a wild stare to someone running past unclothed.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Wild' rearranges STARE into STREA. ER is Elizabeth Regina.
explanation.definitionFit: A streaker runs naked through a public place, often invading a sports pitch.

clue.text: Lose or fail to catch fish, we hear

indicators.note: tells us the phrase is only heard, standing for a word that sounds the same

parts.note: to fail to catch is to miss, and the plaice is a flatfish, together miss plaice

explanation.surface: An angler laments losing a fish or failing to land it.
explanation.walkthrough: 'we hear' turns MISS PLAICE into its sound-alike.
explanation.definitionFit: To misplace something is to put it where it cannot be found, that is, to lose it.

clue.text: Leave behind organised tour — it's heading for Paris

indicators.note: letters that are organised are put into a new arrangement
the heading of a word is its first letter, so only the opening of Paris counts

explanation.surface: A package tour sets off for the French capital, leaving others behind.
explanation.walkthrough: 'organised' rearranges TOUR and IT'S into OUTSTRI; 'heading for' gives P. 'heading for' wants to mean travelling towards.
explanation.definitionFit: To outstrip rivals is to go faster than them, leaving them trailing.

clue.text: Dirty, like a mountain lake?

parts.note: a tarn is a small mountain lake
the suffix -ish means like or somewhat, as in boyish

explanation.surface: A question whether a murky mountain pool is grubby.
explanation.walkthrough: Read as 'a-mountain-lake-ish': the suffix -ish follows the word it qualifies. 'Dirty' is a verb here.
explanation.definitionFit: To tarnish something is to soil or stain it, so to make it dirty.

clue.text: Powder used in metal cannon

indicators.note: the letters are already used in the phrase, lying inside its words

explanation.surface: Gunpowder employed in a metal cannon.
explanation.walkthrough: 'used in' points to letters across metAL Cannon.
explanation.definitionFit: Talc is a soft mineral ground into talcum powder for the skin.

clue.text: Drunk owes me a grand

indicators.note: drunk letters stagger about, so these are rearranged

explanation.surface: A tipsy acquaintance owes the speaker a thousand pounds.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Drunk' rearranges OWES ME into WESOME. 'grand' looks like a thousand pounds but means splendid.
explanation.definitionFit: Grand in its sense of impressive or magnificent is close to awesome.

clue.text: Very famous person's foot?

definitions.meaning: read cryptically, the foot is the leg's end

explanation.surface: A query about a celebrity's foot.
explanation.walkthrough: The answer splits as LEG END, the end of the leg, which is the foot.
explanation.definitionFit: A legend is someone so renowned they become a figure of fame and story.

clue.text: Writer admitting current work is a cinematic life story

indicators.note: admitting means letting in, so the pen takes the other letters inside

parts.note: a Bic is a brand of ballpoint pen, a writer
I is the physics symbol for electric current
OP is short for opus, a work

explanation.surface: An author confesses that their present project is a film about someone's life.
explanation.walkthrough: 'admitting' signals the pen holds the other letters. 'Writer' wants to be an author; it is a brand of ballpoint, and current as I is the physics symbol.
explanation.definitionFit: A biopic is a biographical film, telling a real person's life on screen.

clue.text: Plant wound around end of trellis

indicators.note: the wound word goes around, enclosing the trellis letter

parts.note: to gore is to pierce or wound with a horn

indicators.note: the end of a word is its last letter, so only the final letter of trellis counts

explanation.surface: A garden scene: a climbing plant twisted round a trellis.
explanation.walkthrough: 'end of' gives S; 'around' puts GORE round it. 'wound' reads as twisted, but is the verb for injury.
explanation.definitionFit: Gorse is a spiny yellow-flowered shrub of heaths, also called furze.

clue.text: Gift wrapping I had for chairperson

indicators.note: the gift goes round as a wrapper does, enclosing the other letters

parts.note: a present is a gift
I'd contracts I had

explanation.surface: Someone mentions the gift wrap they had for the boss.
explanation.walkthrough: 'wrapping' signals the gift goes round the contraction I'd, the way paper wraps a present.
explanation.definitionFit: A president presides over a company board or society meeting, a chairperson's role.

clue.text: Arrest mean criminal, e.g. 'Scarface'

parts.note: nick is British slang for arrest

indicators.note: criminal suggests something wrong or crooked, so the letters are rearranged

explanation.surface: Police seize a vicious gangster known as Scarface.
explanation.walkthrough: 'criminal' rearranges MEAN into NAME. Nick for arrest is British slang.
explanation.definitionFit: Scarface was the gangland sobriquet of Al Capone, an example of an informal byname.

clue.text: Expert with brief moment for publicity material

parts.note: a pro is a professional or expert
mo is short for moment, as in just a mo

explanation.surface: A specialist spends a short while producing advertising copy.
explanation.definitionFit: A promo is a promotional item, such as a trailer or advert, used to publicise something.

clue.text: Our King Richard has directions for novelist

parts.note: the reigning British monarch is King Charles III
Dick is a pet form of Richard
E, N and S are compass points, east, north and south

explanation.surface: The British monarch and a man named Richard have instructions for a writer.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Our King' is a British view of the current monarch.
explanation.definitionFit: Charles Dickens wrote Oliver Twist, Great Expectations and many other Victorian novels.
